No, and my earlier "yes" was wrong. From the Moon (~384,000 km) no human-made structure is visible to the naked eye; even Earth's continents appear only as large-scale color and cloud patterns.

Even from low Earth orbit (~400 km) the Wall is barely detectable unaided. It is mostly under ~10 m wide and made of materials that match the surrounding terrain. Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei said in 2003 that he couldn't see it, and astronauts who have photographed it did so with zoom lenses. Cities, highways, and airports are easier to spot from orbit.
